source: tests/fixtures/cost_basis_fop/contract/protocol.json (types and formats; kept equal by the contract test)

formats.IsoDate: YYYY-MM-DD, a calendar or exchange trade date; always 10 characters.
formats.UtcInstant: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ffffffZ in UTC, always six fractional digits and 27 characters, so text order is time order in both readers and in SQLite. Every economic or evidence time uses it: executions, ranges, baselines, observations and as-of instants. It keeps every digit its source gave and pads the rest with zeros; nothing is rounded or truncated, so a fill at 14:30:05.900 is after an as-of of 14:30:05.000000. A source more precise than a microsecond is not cut either: it becomes a TimeRange from the microsecond below to the one above (plan §9.2). An instant is as precise as its source; time.sourceTimeText keeps the original text, and fills a source puts in the same instant are ordered by time.orderEvidence.
formats.RecordedAtUtc: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ, 20 characters: when the server wrote a row, in the form cost_basis_store already stamps createdAtUtc, updatedAtUtc, archivedAtUtc and voidedAtUtc. Bookkeeping only: never an economic time and never compared with a UtcInstant.
